==Overall team records==
{{updated|[[2024 Copa América]]}}

In this ranking [[Three points for a win|3 points are awarded for a win]], 1 for a draw and 0 for a loss. As per statistical convention in football, matches decided in [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] are counted as wins and losses, while matches decided by [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-outs]] are counted as draws. Teams are ranked by total points, then by goal difference, then by goals scored.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://copaamerica.com/en/news/copa-america-all-time-standings-teams-matches-wins-goals-scored|title=Matches, Wins, Goals and More: The All-Time standings of CONMEBOL Copa América™|date=15 August 2024|website=Copa América|access-date=15 August 2024}}</ref>

* [[Dunga]] of {{fb|BRA}}, [[Manuel Seoane]] of {{fb|ARG}}, [[Danilo Alvim]] of {{fb|BRA}} and [[Pedro Cea]] of {{fb|URU}} won the Copa América as a player and also as a coach: Cea won in 1923 and 1924 as a player and in 1942 as a coach; Seoane won in 1925, 1927 and 1929 as a player and in 1937 as a coach; Alvim won in 1949 as a player and in 1963 as a coach (coaching Bolivia); Dunga won in 1989 and 1997 as a player and in 2007 as a coach.
* [[Guillermo Stábile]] {{fbicon|ARG}}, [[Alfio Basile]] {{fbicon|ARG}} and [[Lionel Scaloni]] {{fbicon|ARG}} all had retained the title:  Stábile in 1945, 1946 and 1947 and he is the most retained coach three times; Basile in 1991 and 1993; Scaloni in 2021 and 2024 all of them with {{fb|ARG}}.
* [[José Lago Millán]] {{fbicon|SPA}}, [[Jack Greenwell]]  {{fbicon|ENG}}, [[Danilo Alvim]] {{fbicon|BRA}}, [[Jorge Sampaoli]] {{fbicon|ARG}}, and [[Juan Antonio Pizzi]] {{fbicon|SPA}} won the title as foreign coaches: Millán with Argentina in 1927; Greenwell with Peru in 1939; Alvim with Bolivia in 1963; Sampaoli with Chile in 2015; Pizzi with Chile in 2016.

===Individual records===
*Most goals scored in a single tournament: '''9''' – {{fbicon|BRA|1889}} [[Jair (footballer, born 1921)|Jair]] ([[1949 South American Championship|1949]]), {{fbicon|ARG}} [[Humberto Maschio]] ([[1957 South American Championship|1957]]) and {{fbicon|URU}} [[Javier Ambrois]] ([[1957 South American Championship|1957]])
*Most goals scored in a single match by a player: '''5''' – {{fbicon|URU}} [[Héctor Scarone]] ([[1926 South American Championship|1926]]), {{fbicon|ARG}} [[Juan Marvezzi]] ([[1941 South American Championship|1941]]), {{fbicon|ARG}} [[José Manuel Moreno]] ([[1942 South American Championship|1942]]) and {{fbicon|BRA|1889}} [[Evaristo de Macedo|Evaristo]] ([[1957 South American Championship|1957]])
*Most tournaments scored in: '''6''' – {{fbicon|BRA|1889}} [[Zizinho]] ([[1942 South American Championship|1942]], [[1945 South American Championship|1945]], [[1946 South American Championship|1946]], [[1949 South American Championship|1949]], [[1953 South American Championship|1953]], [[1957 South American Championship|1957]]) and {{fbicon|ARG}} [[Lionel Messi]] ([[2007 Copa América|2007]], [[2015 Copa América|2015]], [[Copa América Centenario|2016]], [[2019 Copa América|2019]], [[2021 Copa América|2021]], [[2024 Copa América|2024]])<ref>{{cite news|title=Lionel Messi matches record with his goal in CONMEBOL Copa América™|url=https://copaamerica.com/en/news/messi-record-copa-america-zizinho-goal-canada|date=10 July 2024|access-date=10 July 2024|website=Copa América}}</ref>
*Most opponents scored against: '''10 –'''  {{fbicon|ARG}} [[Lionel Messi]] (2007–2024)<ref>{{Cite web |title=IFFHS |url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/messi-and-the-copa-america-3789 |access-date=2024-07-31 |website=iffhs.com}}</ref>
*Most overall assists provided: '''18''' – {{fbicon|ARG}} [[Lionel Messi]] (2007–2024)<ref name="telegraphindia.com">{{cite web|title=Copa America: Records broken by Lionel Messi so far|url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/sports/copa-america-records-broken-by-lionel-messi-so-far/cid/1821847|date=9 July 2021|access-date=3 August 2021|website=Telegraph India}}</ref>
*Most assists provided in a single tournament: '''6''' – {{fbicon|BRA}} [[Alex (footballer, born 1977)|Alex]] ([[2004 Copa América|2004]]){{citation needed|date=April 2025}} and {{fbicon|COL}} [[James Rodríguez]] ([[2024 Copa América|2024]])<ref>{{cite news|title=James makes history by surpassing Messi's record in the CONMEBOL Copa America™|url=https://copaamerica.com/en/news/james-record-assists-copa-america-colombia-uruguay|date=11 July 2024|access-date=11 July 2024|website=Copa América}}</ref>
*Most matches won by a player: '''25''' – {{fbicon|ARG}} [[Lionel Messi]] (2007, 2011, 2015, 2016, 2019, 2021, 2024)<ref>{{cite news |date=14 July 2024 |title=Lionel Messi, the new Copa America record holder on wins |url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/wins-record-for-messi-3754 |access-date=19 July 2024 |website=[[IFFHS]]}}</ref>
*Fastest goal scored: '''after 50 seconds''' – {{fbicon|ARG}} [[Darío Franco]] v {{fbicon|BRA}} Brazil ([[1991 Copa América|1991]])<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elgrafico.com.ar/articulo/la-jornada-esta-aqui/40777/cristian-romero-anoto-el-segundo-gol-mas-rapido-de-argentina-en-las-eliminatorias|title=Cristian Romero anoto el segundo gol mas rapido de Argentina en las Eliminatorias|date=8 June 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=1991.07.17 Argentina 3 - Brasil 2 (Partido Completo 60fps - Copa América Chile 1991) {{!}} Full Match {{!}} 3 May 2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jUGAyaur_so |work=YouTube | date=3 May 2023 |publisher=Jwasc92Futbol}}</ref>
*Fastest hat-trick: '''after 10 minutes''' – {{fbicon|ARG}} José Manuel Moreno (1942)
*Youngest player: '''16 years, 1 day''' – {{fbicon|CHI}} [[Humberto Elgueta]] v {{fbicon|BRA}} Brazil ([[1920 South American Championship|1920]])
*Oldest player: '''41 years, 73 days''' – {{fbicon|CHI}} [[Claudio Bravo]] v {{fbicon|ARG}} Argentina ([[2024 Copa América|2024]])<ref>{{cite news |date=22 June 2024 |title=Chile's Bravo becomes oldest player in Copa America history in scoreless draw with Peru |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/copa-america-peru-chile-recap-june-21-1.7243572 |work=CBC Sports |agency=The Associated Press |access-date=5 July 2026}}</ref>
*Youngest goalscorer: '''16 years, 171 days''' – {{fbicon|COL}} [[Johnnier Montaño]] v {{fbicon|ARG}}  Argentina ([[1999 Copa América|1999]])
*Oldest goalscorer: '''37 years, 171 days''' – {{fbicon|URU}} [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] v {{fbicon|CAN}}  Canada ([[2024 Copa América|2024]])
*Most overall direct free kicks scored: '''4''' – '''{{fbicon|ARG}}''' [[Lionel Messi]] (2007–2024)
*Most overall man of the match awards won: '''15''' – {{fbicon|ARG}} [[Lionel Messi]] (2007–2024)
*Most man of the match awards won in a single tournament: '''4''' – '''{{fbicon|ARG}}''' [[Lionel Messi]] (2015 and 2021)
*Most finals played in:  '''5''' – '''{{fbicon|ARG}}''' [[Lionel Messi]] (2007, 2015, 2016, 2021, 2024)<ref>{{Cite web |title=¡Argentina es bicampeón de la CONMEBOL Copa América™! – CONMEBOL |url=https://www.conmebol.com/noticias/argentina-es-bicampeon-de-la-conmebol-copa-america/ |access-date=2024-07-18 |website=www.conmebol.com |date=15 July 2024 }}</ref>
